subject: physics
name: Physics
review_note: Draft written for Quark. Grade levels are typical North American placements and vary by curriculum. Needs review by a subject teacher before it is treated as authoritative.

topics.name: Pushes, pulls and motion
learning_goals: Describe how pushes and pulls change how things move.
Compare the effects of bigger and smaller pushes.

misconceptions.description: Thinks a moving object keeps a push inside it.
misconceptions.example: 'The ball keeps rolling because the push is still in it.'

misconceptions.description: Describes motion without direction or speed words.
misconceptions.example: 'It moved.'

example_problems.prompt: What happens to a toy car if you push it harder?
example_problems.answer: It moves faster and goes farther

topics.name: Light and sound
learning_goals: Explain that sound is made by vibrations and light travels from sources.
Describe shadows and reflection.

misconceptions.description: Thinks we see because light comes out of our eyes.
misconceptions.example: Arrows drawn from the eye to the object

misconceptions.description: Thinks sound travels in space.
misconceptions.example: 'Astronauts can hear an explosion in space.'

example_problems.prompt: Why does a shadow form?

topics.name: Magnets
learning_goals: Describe how magnets attract and repel.
Identify magnetic materials.

misconceptions.description: Thinks all metals are magnetic.
misconceptions.example: 'Aluminium cans stick to magnets.'

misconceptions.description: Thinks a bigger magnet is always stronger.
misconceptions.example: 'The large magnet must be stronger.'

example_problems.prompt: Will two north poles attract or repel?

topics.name: Simple machines
learning_goals: Identify levers, pulleys, inclined planes, wedges, screws and wheels and axles.
Explain how machines trade force for distance.

misconceptions.description: Thinks a machine reduces the work needed.
misconceptions.example: 'The ramp means less work.'

misconceptions.description: Misidentifies the fulcrum.
misconceptions.example: Calls the load point of a wheelbarrow the fulcrum.

example_problems.prompt: How does a ramp make lifting a box easier?
example_problems.answer: You push with less force over a longer distance

topics.name: Forms of energy and energy transfer
learning_goals: Identify forms of energy and energy transformations.
Explain that energy is conserved.
key_concepts: Kinetic, potential, thermal, electrical, chemical, light, sound

misconceptions.description: Thinks energy is used up or disappears.
misconceptions.example: 'The battery's energy is gone forever.'

misconceptions.description: Calls force, power and energy the same thing.
misconceptions.example: 'The car has a lot of force energy.'

example_problems.prompt: Describe the energy transformation in a flashlight.

topics.name: Electricity and simple circuits
learning_goals: Build and draw simple series and parallel circuits.
Identify conductors and insulators.

misconceptions.description: Thinks current is used up by bulbs.
misconceptions.example: 'Less current flows back to the battery.'

misconceptions.description: Draws circuits with incorrect or missing symbols.
misconceptions.example: Draws a bulb as a resistor without labels

example_problems.prompt: If one bulb in a series circuit breaks, what happens to the others?
example_problems.answer: They go out because the circuit is broken

topics.name: Balanced and unbalanced forces
learning_goals: Use force diagrams to show balanced and unbalanced forces.
Relate net force to changes in motion.

misconceptions.description: Thinks a constant-speed object has an unbalanced force.
misconceptions.example: 'The car moves at constant speed because the engine force is bigger.'

misconceptions.description: Adds a 'force of motion'.
misconceptions.example: Draws a forward arrow for a sliding puck

example_problems.prompt: A 20 N push right and 5 N friction left act on a box. What is the net force?

topics.name: Heat and temperature
learning_goals: Distinguish heat and temperature.
Explain conduction, convection and radiation.

misconceptions.description: Thinks cold flows into warm objects.
misconceptions.example: 'The ice puts cold into the drink.'

misconceptions.description: Uses heat and temperature as the same thing.
misconceptions.example: 'The bath has more temperature than the cup.'

example_problems.prompt: Why does a metal spoon in hot soup get hot?
example_problems.answer: Thermal energy is conducted from the soup through the metal

topics.name: Motion in one dimension
learning_goals: Describe motion with distance, displacement, speed, velocity and acceleration.
Use motion graphs and kinematic equations.
key_concepts: Slope of d-t is velocity; slope of v-t is acceleration

misconceptions.description: Thinks zero velocity means zero acceleration.
misconceptions.example: 'At the top of its flight the ball has no acceleration.'

misconceptions.description: Reads a v-t graph as a position graph.
misconceptions.example: Says the object moves backward when v decreases

misconceptions.description: Gives a velocity without direction.
misconceptions.example: v = 12 m/s

example_problems.prompt: A car speeds up from 5 m/s to 25 m/s in 4 s. Find its acceleration.
How far does an object fall from rest in 3 s (g = 9.8 m/s^2)?

topics.name: Newton's laws
learning_goals: Apply Newton's three laws to everyday and quantitative problems.
Draw free-body diagrams and use F_net = ma.
key_concepts: Action-reaction pairs act on different objects

misconceptions.description: Says third-law pairs cancel.
misconceptions.example: 'The horse can't pull the cart because the forces cancel.'

misconceptions.description: Includes forces acting on other objects.
misconceptions.example: Adds the force the box exerts on the floor

misconceptions.description: Uses mass in grams in F = ma.
misconceptions.example: F = 500 x 2 for a 500 g cart

example_problems.prompt: A net force of 30 N acts on a 6 kg cart. Find its acceleration.

topics.name: Work, energy and power
learning_goals: Calculate work, kinetic and gravitational potential energy and power.
Use conservation of energy to solve problems.

misconceptions.description: Leaves out an energy store or transfer.
misconceptions.example: Ignores thermal energy lost to friction

misconceptions.description: Forgets the 1/2 or the square in kinetic energy.
misconceptions.example: Ek = mv^2

example_problems.prompt: A 2 kg ball is dropped from 5 m. Find its speed just before it lands (g = 9.8 m/s^2).

topics.name: Waves and sound
learning_goals: Describe transverse and longitudinal waves.
Use v = f(lambda) and describe interference and resonance.

misconceptions.description: Thinks a higher frequency makes a wave travel faster in the same medium.
misconceptions.example: 'High notes reach you first.'

misconceptions.description: Uses period where frequency is needed.
misconceptions.example: v = T x lambda

example_problems.prompt: A wave has frequency 50 Hz and wavelength 4 m. Find its speed.

topics.name: Light, reflection and refraction
learning_goals: Apply the law of reflection and Snell's law.
Draw ray diagrams for mirrors and lenses.
key_concepts: Angle of incidence = angle of reflection

misconceptions.description: Measures angles from the surface instead of the normal.
misconceptions.example: Angle of incidence 30 degrees from the mirror surface

misconceptions.description: Draws a ray through the focus incorrectly.
misconceptions.example: Ray parallel to the axis refracts through the near-side focus

example_problems.prompt: Light enters glass (n = 1.50) from air at 30 degrees to the normal. Find the angle of refraction.

topics.name: Current, voltage, resistance and Ohm's law
learning_goals: Use V = IR and power P = VI.
Find equivalent resistance in series and parallel circuits.

misconceptions.description: Adds parallel resistors as if in series.
misconceptions.example: 6 ohm and 3 ohm in parallel = 9 ohm

misconceptions.description: Thinks current decreases after each resistor in series.
misconceptions.example: '2 A before the bulb, 1 A after.'

example_problems.prompt: Find the equivalent resistance of 6 ohm and 3 ohm in parallel.
A 12 V battery drives current through a 4 ohm resistor. Find the current.

topics.name: Momentum and collisions
learning_goals: Use p = mv and impulse.
Apply conservation of momentum to collisions and explosions.

misconceptions.description: Ignores direction when adding momenta.
misconceptions.example: Adds momenta of objects moving toward each other

misconceptions.description: Changes the sign convention part-way through.
misconceptions.example: Takes right as positive, then a leftward velocity as positive

example_problems.prompt: A 2 kg cart at 3 m/s hits and sticks to a stationary 1 kg cart. Find their speed.

topics.name: Two-dimensional motion and vectors
learning_goals: Resolve and add vectors.
Solve projectile motion problems.
key_concepts: Independence of horizontal and vertical motion

misconceptions.description: Adds magnitudes of perpendicular vectors.
misconceptions.example: 3 m east + 4 m north = 7 m

misconceptions.description: Thinks a projectile has a horizontal force.
misconceptions.example: Draws a forward force on a ball in flight

example_problems.prompt: A ball is thrown horizontally at 10 m/s from a 20 m cliff. How long is it in the air (g = 9.8 m/s^2)?

topics.name: Circular motion and gravitation
learning_goals: Analyse uniform circular motion with centripetal acceleration and force.
Apply Newton's law of universal gravitation.
key_concepts: Centripetal force is a net force, not a new force

misconceptions.description: Adds an outward centrifugal force in an inertial frame.
misconceptions.example: Draws an outward force on a car going round a curve

misconceptions.description: Uses the wrong value or power of ten for G.

example_problems.prompt: A 0.5 kg ball moves in a circle of radius 2 m at 4 m/s. Find the centripetal force.

topics.name: Magnetic fields and electromagnetism
learning_goals: Describe magnetic fields around magnets and currents.
Explain motors, generators and induction.

misconceptions.description: Applies the hand rule with the wrong hand or current direction.
misconceptions.example: Uses the left hand for conventional current

misconceptions.description: Thinks a transformer creates energy.
misconceptions.example: 'A step-up transformer increases power.'

example_problems.prompt: What happens to induced current if a magnet is moved faster into a coil?

topics.name: Electric charge and electric fields
learning_goals: Use Coulomb's law and describe electric fields.
Relate field, force and potential difference.

misconceptions.description: Forgets to square the distance.
misconceptions.example: F = kq1q2 / r

misconceptions.description: Adds field strengths from two charges without direction.
misconceptions.example: Fields from opposite sides added as if parallel

example_problems.prompt: If the distance between two charges doubles, what happens to the force between them?
example_problems.answer: It becomes one quarter as large

topics.name: Atomic and nuclear physics
learning_goals: Describe radioactive decay and half-life.
Write nuclear equations and explain fission and fusion.

misconceptions.description: Treats decay as linear, subtracting the same amount each half-life.
misconceptions.example: 100 g after two half-lives = 0 g

misconceptions.description: Does not balance mass or atomic numbers in a nuclear equation.
misconceptions.example: Alpha decay of U-238 gives Th-238

example_problems.prompt: A 80 g sample has a half-life of 5 days. How much remains after 15 days?
